title: Back in the Basie studio after the hospital; Sonny Payne
summary: After leaving hospital he sat in on a Basie date, and Basie kept the flashier Sonny Payne.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Well, when you got out of hospital, and you were ready to play again, you did a spell with Lena Horne?
Oh, yes. Well, when I got out of the hospital, I think Basie came back into town and Sonny was playing with the band.
Sonny Payne.

Sonny Payne. And they made a record date and I went down and made a session. And not that day but about, I'd say, about a month later I made a session with Basie because something happened. Sonny didn't show up, and I don't know what happened, but he wasn't there. And they was out looking for a drummer, and I just happened to be walking down Broadway, and the valet saw me and said, "Good, just the guy I want to see." And went by Columbia Studio and -- yeah, Columbia Studio.
Yeah.
And I made a date with him.
That was nice. Freddie was mighty glad to see you show up?
Yeah. Everybody was glad to see me.
Yeah.
But --
They've had their troubles, haven't
Yeah, sure.
For a band that relies on its rhythm section.
Yeah, they had a lot of trouble.
Yeah.
But he was a good drummer, though, for the band. He was flashy, good flashy.
So the action wasn't so much on swinging the band as on the show.
Well, Basie basically, liked a lot of flash.
Yeah. Well, he felt it sold.
Yeah, sure, sure.
Yeah.

I know he wrote me while I was in the hospital and said that Sonny was doing a good job, and he think he'd make a good drummer with the band, good flashy drummer, and that he was going to keep him with the band while I was still in the hospital.
Yeah, so --
That was all right.
Well, it's what he felt he required. That may not be what the band felt, but that's what --
No, because it was kind of, as they
say, a dirty -- looked like he waited till everybody got sick or was in the hospital or something like that before he fired them. And even with Charlie Fowlkes. Charlie Fowlkes fell and broke his --
I remember, and was out for ages, wasn't he?
Yeah, and he didn't hire him back. Marshal Royal, when something happened to him, he had to go to the hospital, and he got the other --
In other words, don't get sick.
Well, that was the way it was. Don't get sick, see. But I had always told him that if he felt that he wanted to get another drummer, just let me know, one of those things.
What did you feel about the spirit in the band, as far as the band went? Was it enjoyable?
When I played with them?
Yeah.
Oh, it was fine with me. I enjoyed playing with the band.
But there were cliques and things, weren't there?
Well, I --
Or you didn't have to be aware of them.
They could have had cliques. I'm
quite sure they had a few cliques in the band.
Yeah.
Certain ones that wanted a Sonny in the band.
Yeah.
And which I found out later, it was.
Well, tell me, I'd like to know, if you don't mind saying.
What? No, I don't mind saying.
Who were the guys?

Which was told to me, that, like, even Charlie Fowlkes, he told me Basie that Sonny was the better drummer and the more showman and like that. And then come to find out he was one of the guys that got let out, too.
That's funny, isn't it?
Yeah, it was real funny, you know?
Yeah, that is funny.
But that was all right with me.
Yeah.
